topic: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem and the Stolen Necklace Problem
target_audience: Undergraduate students in mathematics or computer science

sections.title: Intuitive Prerequisite: The Antipodal Mapping
lecture_lines: A sphere has pairs of opposite, antipodal points.
Imagine points on the North and South Poles.
Antipodal points are exactly on the opposite side.
animations: Create a sphere using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/globe.svg] (#FFFFFF) with two antipodal points (#FF0000) appearing.
Rotate the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/globe.svg] (#000000 background) showing the two points (#00FF00).
Draw a connection line (#FFFF00) between the two antipodal points on the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/globe.svg].

sections.title: The Core Concept: Borsuk-Ulam Theorem
lecture_lines: Borsuk-Ulam maps n-spheres to n-dimensional space.
It guarantees a mapping of at least one antipodal pair.
Temperature and pressure match at two opposite points.
animations: Visualize a sphere being flattened onto a 2D plane (#FFFFFF) next to a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/thermometer.svg].
Animate two antipodal points mapping to one spot (#FF5733).
Apply a pulse effect (#FFC300) at the overlapping points.
Draw a path (#33FF57) highlighting the continuous mapping.
Fade all elements into the black background (#000000) alongside a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/barometer.svg].

sections.title: The Stolen Necklace Problem
lecture_lines: Thieves divide a necklace with different beads.
They want an equal share of every bead type.
We can cut the necklace at most k times.
animations: Display a necklace [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/necklace.svg] line with colorful bead [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bead.svg] circles (#FFFFFF).
Animate a cut separator splitting the necklace [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/necklace.svg] segments (#FF5733).
Highlight segments showing equal bead [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bead.svg] values for thieves (#33FF57).

sections.title: Bridging Theory and Problem
lecture_lines: Model the necklace as an interval on a sphere.
Borsuk-Ulam proves a fair division must exist.
The exact cut points are hard to find.
animations: Map the necklace beads [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/beads.svg] onto a spherical surface [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] (#FFFFFF).
Move the beads [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/beads.svg] along the sphere to show distribution (#FFC300).
Highlight the antipodal points of the necklace [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/necklace.svg] matching for fair division (#33FF57).

sections.title: Conclusion and Summary
lecture_lines: Borsuk-Ulam is a powerful existence theorem in topology.
It guarantees that fair divisions are always possible.
Topology proves the existence of impossible solutions.
animations: Display a summary of the sphere [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] and points (#FFFFFF).
Display the Borsuk-Ulam theorem text label (#FF5733).
Fade out the final visualization of the sphere [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] to black (#33FF57).
